intro: Dental hygienists combine clinical skill, patient teaching and precision. The closest of the 25 careers below are Nuclear Medicine Technologists and medical sonographers, both at a 74% skill match; nuclear medicine pays a BLS May 2025 median of $101,370, or 3% more than the $98,100 hygienists earn.
why_it_works: Each appointment means cleaning and examining teeth, spotting problems and teaching patients better habits. O*NET rates social perceptiveness and service orientation at 3.12 out of 5 for this job. Imaging, sonography and surgical support use the same clinical focus. Because your pay is already high, only 2 matches pay more. Most need no extra degree, but many need a new certificate or license.
tips: Imaging careers are the closest move in pay: MRI technologists earn $95,480 and sonographers $96,590.
Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, which is 50% more, but usually need a bachelor's degree.
If you want to leave patient care, ask dental supply companies about education or sales roles.

faq.q: What jobs can former dental hygienists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Nuclear Medicine Technologists (74%), medical sonographers (74%) and MRI technologists (71%), based on O*NET 31.0. Surgical Assistants are 70% matched but earn $66,800, which is 32% less than the $98,100 hygienist median, so imaging is usually the better-paid direction.

faq.q: Which careers for dental hygienists pay more?
faq.a: Only 2 of the 25 matches pay more. Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470 (50% more) and Nuclear Medicine Technologists $101,370 (3% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Nuclear Monitoring Technicians earn $110,240 for their broader group, and dosimetry usually needs a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Do dental hygienists need more education to switch?
faq.a: Usually not a degree. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than hygienists already have, including all of the top 10. An associate degree is common, held by 63% of workers in the closest match, though imaging jobs need their own certification.

faq.q: What skills should dental hygienists learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, systems analysis, quality control analysis and social perceptiveness. Instructing already rates 3 out of 5 for hygienists in O*NET, so learning to run imaging equipment is the main step toward other clinical roles.
